messages:
ashwin: Heads-up: proposal to add a 'ProSeries' routing policy that prioritizes low-latency variants in us-* regions, with a soft quota and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant when capacity is constrained. Sketch below. Want alignment on API shape + console UX before we ship canary.

maria: Sounds reasonable. Quick Q: what exactly do you mean by soft vs hard quota behavior? soft -> throttle? redirect? 429?

ashwin: Soft = don't 429; instead we switch routing to fallback variants after the tenant exceeds the configured window limit, still count usage for billing/telemetry. Hard = reject with 429 once limit hit. Proposed policy JSON (draft):

```
{
  "tier": "proseries",
  "quota": {"mode":"soft","window_s":3600,"limit":100000},
  "routing": [
    {"variant":"redwood-l3-lowlat","priority":100},
    {"variant":"redwood-l3-std","priority":50,"fallback":true}
  ],
  "fallback_policy": {"on_capacity":"route_to_lower_variant","on_error":"retry_with_backoff"}
}
```

kevin: API shape looks nice. A couple of asks: (1) add policy_version metadata so we can roll configs, (2) admin endpoint should support force_fallback flag for testing. Also: how will console surface per-tenant burn rate? we need panel(s): quota remaining, projected exhaustion time, fallback events count, avg latency delta when fallback used.

zoe: +1 to those panels. UX note: add a short 'grace' indicator (last 5m) and a canary toggle in the console to enable this policy for a subset of tenants. Also link to rollout controls (percentage rollout / tenant list).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary toggle enabled for staging at 2024-01-12T10:23:00Z :rocket:

ashwin: Implementation notes: runtime evaluation order = tenant tier -> region affinity -> variant availability. If preferred variant unavailable or capacity-exceeded, consult fallback_policy. On soft quota transition we should still decrement quota for the attempt (so billing stays accurate). Telemetry we need: routing_decision{tenant,tier,region,chosen_variant,reason} and fallback_event{tenant,from_variant,to_variant}.

maria: tagging @jon (product) for SLA implications. Legal/infosec will want fallback logs for auditability.

jon: SLA check: ProSeries should remain at 99.9% regional latency SLO. Fallbacks are OK but must be visible in the console and in daily rollups. I'm okay with soft-by-default for canary.

kevin: implementation detail: admin endpoint sample payload for testing/QA:

```
POST /admin/policies/activate
{
  "policy_id": "proseries-v1",
  "force_fallback": true,
  "canary_tenants": ["tenant-123","tenant-456"]
}
```

ashwin: Rollout plan: week 1: staging canary (10 tenants) + heavy chaos tests, week 2: expand to 50 tenants in prod canary, monitor 1) fallback_rate, 2) avg p95 latency delta, 3) billing discrepancy. Rollback triggers: fallback_rate > 5% sustained for 10m OR p95 latency increase > 20% vs baseline.

zoe: I'll mock console panels and flows today and post screenshots. Also will add a small tooltip explaining soft vs hard and what 'fallback' means.

maria: I'll add an e2e test that simulates regional capacity loss and asserts fallback events are emitted, plus a test for hard quota 429 behavior.

ashwin: Thanks — I'll open an RFC + API PR with the JSON schema and runtime change-set, and tag eng-sre for rollout windows.

deploy-bot: RFC created: https://rfc.internal/redwood/proseries-routing-2024-v1 (staging link)
